scope.reviewed_media: Actual encoded animated WebP and both light/dark GIF files plus per-frame WebP files
not_reviewed: Live browser playback at intended widget size
Runtime translation, collision, input interruption or state-machine transitions

tools: Node.js sharp for decode, proportional resize and mechanical contact-sheet composition
view_image for visual review of all ten WebP contact sheets and all ten actual-GIF contact sheets
method.visual_layout: For each action, eight decoded frames at 256x256 arranged 4x2 on a light background and again on a dark background.
method.frame_order_check: Each decoded animation frame was compared against all eight frame files at 64x64; closest match was the same 1-based source frame for every reviewed WebP and GIF page.
method.timings: Read actual frame delay arrays and loop metadata from each encoded file. Temporal smoothness conclusions are limited to ordered-frame inspection and timing metadata, not claimed live playback.
method.quantitative_note: MAE and bounding boxes detect file/sequence/crop issues; they are not a biological motion or perceptual smoothness certification.

global_observations: All ten WebP files decode as eight 512x512 RGBA pages with transparent background pixels.
All twenty GIF files decode as eight 320x320 pages; decoded GIF pixels are fully opaque because these are deliberate light/dark flattened variants.
All decoded sequences preserve order 1 through 8 and the GIF/WebP delays agree.
No alpha>128 subject pixels touch the outer two-pixel frame boundary in the eighty reviewed WebP pages. Visual review also found no cropped paw, ear or tail silhouette.
No extra limb, false lettering, prop or colored-alpha debris was observed on the reviewed actual light/dark composites.
The asset set consists of eight keyframes per action. It should not be described as rigged animation, 60 fps authored motion or a biologically validated movement simulation.

observations: Frames 2–3 clearly change from crouch to push-off; frames 4–5 tuck the paws in the air; frame 6 extends toward landing; frames 7–8 settle.
Actual encoded frames have visible vertical flight clearance and complete ears, paws and tail on both light and dark backgrounds.
limits: Head angle and apparent face size vary slightly between takeoff, tucked and settled poses; this is not a rigid character rig.
Only eight authored poses are present. The observed phase order supports a jump, but no real-time browser playback or 60 fps interpolation was evaluated.
actions.loop: Frame 8 returns to a similar grounded pose as frame 1. The seam is not pixel-identical; the final 650 ms hold softens the restart.

observations: The sequence shows sit, forepaw reach, raised hips/chest-down stretch, rounded back and return to sit.
